There are 360 people in my school.  15 take calculus, physics, and chemistry, and 15 don't take any of them.  180 take calculus.  Twice as many students take chemistry as take physics.  75 take both calculus and chemistry, and 75 take both physics and chemistry.  Only 30 take both physics and calculus.  How many students take physics?

Give only the final answer.

Let $C$ be the set of students taking calculus, $P$ be the set of students taking physics, and $H$ be the set of students taking chemistry.
We are given the following information:
- Total number of students $N = 360$.
- Number of students taking none of the subjects: $|(C \cup P \cup H)^c| = 15$.
- Number of students taking all three subjects: $|C \cap P \cap H| = 15$.
- Number of students taking calculus: $|C| = 180$.
- Number of students taking chemistry is twice the number taking physics: $|H| = 2|P|$.
- Number of students taking both calculus and chemistry: $|C \cap H| = 75$.
- Number of students taking both physics and chemistry: $|P \cap H| = 75$.
- Number of students taking both physics and calculus: $|P \cap C| = 30$.

First, we calculate the number of students taking at least one of the subjects:
$|C \cup P \cup H| = N - |(C \cup P \cup H)^c| = 360 - 15 = 345$.

Using the Principle of Inclusion-Exclusion for three sets:
$|C \cup P \cup H| = |C| + |P| + |H| - (|C \cap P| + |C \cap H| + |P \cap H|) + |C \cap P \cap H|$

Substitute the known values into the equation:
$345 = 180 + |P| + 2|P| - (30 + 75 + 75) + 15$

Simplify the equation:
$345 = 180 + 3|P| - 180 + 15$
$345 = 3|P| + 15$
$330 = 3|P|$
$|P| = 110$

Thus, 110 students take physics.

FINAL ANSWER: 110
